title: Apple details Secure Exclaves audio/video privacy and recording-indicator checks
summary: Apple published a Nov. 12 explainer on Secure Exclaves, an isolated security environment that processes audio and video so the main system and apps in ambient-sensing modes receive only the recognition results they need rather than raw data. Apple says the architecture is used in HomeView&\#x27;s face and sound recognition and in the iPhone 18 Pro privacy indicator. On the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple says dedicated hardware verifies the microphone dot&\#x27;s color, brightness, and visibility before audio can enter the main system, and that relevant Siri audio sessions must keep the dot displayed for at least three seconds. These are Apple&\#x27;s described mechanisms; the supplied report does not include independent verification or API-level details.
